page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-2GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Premium family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. Memory capacity is limited to 2.0 GB, yielding 1.0 GB per core. The server is equipped with 50 GB of local SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. It does not feature a GPU.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance alongside moderate multi-core capabilities. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance ranks in the top tier (top 10%), and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also achieve top-tier results. However, multi-core stress-ng performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average category. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU physics tests show weaker performance, placing in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the poor category (bottom 10%), though raw memory bandwidth remains average.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a budget-friendly entry point with high single-thread execution speeds relative to its shared CPU allocation. The primary tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:1 and poor overall memory performance, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications. Database operations also show weaker performance (bottom 25%). Consequently, this configuration is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, static content delivery, and simple background tasks that do not require large memory footprints or sustained multi-core execution.
